Wall-clock/ratio harness; reps=5 real coordinator solves make this slower than the count-only harnesses.

finding.title: Home Assistant stop waits out an in-flight solve before reaping the solve worker
finding.claim: The EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener from async_register_worker_shutdown, fired 0.1 s into a real solve, returns only when the solve does (0.93 of the solve's duration), against 0.008 s with no solve in flight.
finding.mechanism: _shutdown_process_pool takes the module-global _PROCESS_LOCK, which _run_in_process holds for the whole transport round trip (pickle.dump .. pickle.load, i.e. the entire solve). The reap therefore queues behind the solve instead of terminating the child; on a Pi (30-70 s solves, or the D1-s2-02 runaway) that is how long a restart stalls.

evidence.unit: stop latency / solve duration (median of 5; min 0.843, max 1.017)
evidence.machine: B4 cloud container (Linux 6.18, x86_64), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: shared B4 during fan-out, 0 concurrent stress.py; ratio metric, absolutes provisional

perturbation.change: --perturb unlocked_reap: coordinator._PROCESS_LOCK rebound to a fresh Lock for the stop call only (a reap that does not queue behind the transport lock)

finding.metric_definition: Wall time for the stop listener to return when fired 0.1 s into a real coordinator solve, divided by that solve's own duration measured in the same session.
finding.phenomenon_property: Reaping the solve worker at stop never waits for a solve in flight: the stop reap completes in bounded time independent of solve duration.

null_control.note: same listener, same session, no solve in flight

reproduction_steps: Set up an entry on a real loop with a ThreadPoolExecutor
Await the registered EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener: it returns when the solve finishes
finding.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._shutdown_process_pool: grab the worker handle without waiting on the transport lock (or kill the child first so the in-flight pickle.load fails fast), keeping the lock only for the handle swap.
